scenarios.debrief: Evenly shared chores make daily life lighter for everyone and cut quiet resentment.
scenarios.relearn: Sharing chores evenly lifts everyone; equality at home helps all.

scenarios.hook: A classmate says 'this fairness stuff isn't my problem to fix'.

steps.prompt: He says it as the class forms a fairness committee. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him fine, and leave it to those who care
options.then: He nods, relieved, and heads off to the canteen.

options.text: Invite him in: "A fairer batch helps you too"
options.then: He hesitates. "Helps me how?"

options.text: Tell him he's part of the problem if he sits out
options.then: He scowls. "I never said I was against it."

options.text: Ask the class rep to go and convince him
options.then: The rep has a word with him, and he feels singled out.

steps.why: Inviting him in makes it his project too, instead of a job for other people.

steps.prompt: The committee opens its first meeting with mostly girls. What do you do?

options.text: Ask a few of the boys to join and help shape it
options.then: Four boys come to the next meeting, and two volunteer to take tasks.

options.text: Carry on, since the people who care are here
options.then: The plan looks sound. Half the class stays outside the conversation.

options.text: Say the boys are welcome, but you won't chase them
options.then: Only one boy walks in.

options.text: Keep the first few meetings for girls only
options.then: The plan forms without boys, who later say it wasn't for them.

steps.why: Asking the boys directly widens the group beyond whoever turned up first.

steps.prompt: A month on, a boy in your class suggests a 'respect week'. The committee says it sounds soft. What do you do?

options.text: Agree it sounds a little soft and move on
options.then: The idea fades, and he sits back quietly.

options.text: Take over the planning and run it yourself
options.then: The week is planned fast, without the boy who proposed it.

options.text: Suggest he plan it alone, since it's his idea
options.then: He agrees, then finds nobody turns up to help.

options.text: Back it and suggest one concrete activity to begin
options.then: The group adds a chore-swap day. "Okay, let's try it."

steps.why: Backing his idea with one concrete step makes it easy to try.

steps.prompt: Some weeks on, the classmate who said it wasn't his problem asks if he can help with the committee's next project. What do you say?

options.text: Say the team is already full for the next one
options.then: He shrugs and walks off, a little deflated.

options.text: Say he's welcome to come and just watch
options.then: He comes, watches, and leaves early, unsure what to do.

options.text: Say yes, and give him a real job on the next project
options.then: He grins. "Give me the poster work. I'm good at that."

options.text: Say you'll check with the others and let him know
options.then: The message never gets sent, and he assumes it was a polite no.

steps.why: Giving him a real role turns a change of mind into lasting involvement.

scenarios.debrief: Inviting people in beats letting them opt out. Fairness works best as a shared project.
scenarios.relearn: Equality is built with everyone. Invite people in, because it helps them too.

scenarios.hook: A teammate grabs all the visible credit and you could do the same.

steps.prompt: After the demo, your teammate takes the praise. The teacher asks who built what. What do you do?

options.text: Grab your share of credit too, since he did
options.then: You both talk over each other, and the teacher sighs.

options.text: Share credit openly: name every person's part
options.then: The teacher writes four names. Your teammate looks a little sheepish.

options.text: Say nothing, since it isn't worth a fight
options.then: The teacher notes one name. Two teammates look away.

options.text: Correct him sharply in front of the whole class
options.then: He turns red, and the class falls silent.

steps.why: Sharing credit openly builds trust, and it lifts you along with the team.

steps.prompt: The next project starts. Your teammate asks who should present. What do you say?

options.text: Suggest a rotation so each person presents something
options.then: He says, "Okay, fair." Everyone picks a slot.

options.text: Say you'll present all of it this time to be safe
options.then: You do it alone, and the team relaxes into watching.

options.text: Say let him present, as usual. It's easier
options.then: He presents and takes all the praise again.

options.text: Say to pick whoever speaks best, to save time
options.then: The loudest voice wins, and two teammates don't present at all.

steps.why: A rotation shares the visible work so credit follows effort.

steps.prompt: At the final review, the teacher praises the slides but never mentions Meenal's data work. She looks let down. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her privately that she should speak up next time
options.then: She nods, but the teacher's notes still leave her out.

options.text: Say it's only marks, so it's not worth minding
options.then: She nods, and the disappointment just sits there.

options.text: Promise to give her credit on the next project
options.then: She thanks you. The next project starts, and the promise slips.

options.text: Tell the teacher what she built, in front of the team
options.then: The teacher smiles at her. She sits a little taller.

steps.why: Naming her work in front of the team gives credit where it's due, straight away.

scenarios.debrief: Sharing credit isn't a loss. It builds trust and lifts the whole team, you included.
scenarios.relearn: Sharing credit grows trust and lifts everyone; it isn't zero-sum.

scenarios.hook: An uncle insists 'a son who helps in the kitchen is being made soft'.

steps.prompt: He says it at family lunch while your cousin is chopping onions. What do you do?

options.text: Laugh and agree to keep the peace at lunch
options.then: Your cousin puts the knife down, and Uncle looks satisfied.

options.text: Tell him he's stuck in the past and out of touch
options.then: Uncle's jaw tightens, and your aunt changes the subject sharply.

options.text: Say he's learning skills he'll use his whole life
options.then: Uncle grunts. "Skills? He can hire a cook."

options.text: Take the knife and finish the chopping yourself
options.then: Your cousin sits down, and the kitchen work goes on as before.

steps.why: Shared care teaches skills and closeness. It isn't weakness.

steps.prompt: Later your cousin says he likes cooking but fears college boys will tease him. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's smarter to hide it from his college friends
options.then: He nods, and keeps his cooking quiet from then on.

options.text: Say he can like what he likes, and cook with you
options.then: He laughs with relief. "Sunday? I'll teach you biryani."

options.text: Say nobody at college would even notice or care
options.then: He looks unconvinced. The worry stays.

options.text: Say he should stop cooking if it bothers him that much
options.then: He shrugs, and cooks far less after that.

steps.why: Backing his interest, and cooking alongside him, tells him it isn't weakness.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, your cousin makes the dal for a family lunch, and Uncle asks who made it. What do you say?

options.text: Say it was your cousin, and he made it himself
options.then: Uncle chews, then asks for a second helping.

options.text: Say your aunt made it, to avoid another scene
options.then: Uncle nods, and your cousin's work goes uncredited.

options.text: Say you'll tell him later, once he has finished
options.then: Uncle leaves the table. The moment passes.

options.text: Say "See, even a boy can cook" and smile
options.then: Uncle grunts, and your cousin winces at the word 'even'.

steps.why: Naming who cooked it lets the family see the skill, not the stereotype.

scenarios.debrief: A son sharing care gains skills and closeness. Rigid roles cost boys too.
scenarios.relearn: Sharing care frees boys from rigid roles; it's a gain, not weakness.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Imran has been bingeing reels that mock anything to do with equality.
scenarios.setup: You're chatting after class.

steps.prompt: Imran says: "Feminism just wants men to lose. You know it."

options.text: "Why are you always so defensive about this?"
options.then: Imran crosses his arms. "I'm not defensive. You are."

options.text: "It's fairness for all of us. Nobody has to lose."
options.then: Imran frowns. "Then why does it sound like blame?"

options.text: "Yeah, you might be right on that one."
options.then: Imran grins. "See? And don't get me started on jobs."

options.text: "Not now. I've got an exam tomorrow."
options.then: He nods. "Fine. But I'm not done with this."

steps.why: Saying nobody has to lose lowers the heat and keeps him talking.

steps.prompt: A few days later Imran says: "Jobs are limited. Every woman hired means one less man."

options.text: "It's not a fixed pie. Fairer teams often do better."
options.then: He thinks. "Better how? Like better ideas?"

options.text: "That's just how it is. Let's not get into it."
options.then: He shrugs. "So you agree with me."

options.text: "You're just scared of the competition. Admit it."
options.then: Imran flushes. "I'm not scared of anyone."

options.text: "Maybe. I don't really know about that."
options.then: Imran shrugs. The claim stands.

steps.why: Fairer teams often do better, so one person's gain isn't another's loss.

steps.prompt: The next week he says: "My sister says I never help at home. Is that feminism too?"

options.text: "She's right, and you've been lazy."
options.then: He reddens and goes silent.

options.text: "Your sister sounds a bit bossy, to be honest with you."
options.then: Imran laughs, and the real issue stays untouched.

options.text: "Don't ask me. Ask her yourself."
options.then: He shrugs. "She'll just shout."

options.text: "It's fairness. Sharing the housework helps you both."
options.then: He nods. "Fine. I'll start with the dishes."

steps.why: Linking fairness to a lighter shared load makes it a gain, not a blame game.

scenarios.relearn: Reframe equality as fairness for everyone, men included; nobody loses.

scenarios.hook: At a family dinner, your aunt keeps shooing the boys out of the kitchen.
scenarios.setup: Your younger cousin Arjun is setting the table.

steps.prompt: Aunty says: "Why should boys do housework? That's not for them."

options.text: "You're right. I'll lay the table myself."
options.then: Aunty nods. Arjun slips away, and you work alone.

options.text: "That's such an old-fashioned thing to say, Aunty."
options.then: Aunty stiffens. "Old-fashioned? I raised three children."

options.text: "It teaches life skills and lightens the load for all."
options.then: Aunty pauses. "Skills? Hmm. He does burn the tea."

options.text: "Let's not start this over dinner, Aunty."
options.then: Aunty shrugs, and the dishes pile up as always.

steps.why: Naming life skills and a lighter home speaks to her care for the boys.

steps.prompt: Later Aunty says quietly: "Arjun goes to a hostel next year. The boys there will laugh if he cooks."

options.text: "Then he should hide it from them, Aunty."
options.then: Aunty nods. Arjun learns that cooking is something to hide.

options.text: "Lots of boys cook in hostels and flats. It's a skill."
options.then: She thinks. "True. Ravi makes good omelettes."

options.text: "Let them laugh. Who cares what those boys think?"
options.then: Aunty frowns. "He cares. That's the problem."

options.text: "Maybe you're right. Let's leave it, Aunty."
options.then: Aunty smiles, and the chores go back to the women as before.

steps.why: Showing that cooking is a normal skill answers her worry about teasing.

steps.prompt: At the festival, Aunty asks: "Who will help me in the kitchen?"

options.text: "Arjun and I will. He can chop while I stir."
options.then: Arjun grins. Aunty hands him a knife and keeps an eye on him.

options.text: "The girls will, as always, Aunty."
options.then: The girls head for the kitchen. Arjun goes back to his phone.

options.text: "I'll do it all myself. Arjun can rest."

options.text: "Ask Arjun. I'm a bit busy right now."
options.then: Arjun shrugs and fumbles it. Aunty mutters, "See? Boys can't."

steps.why: Naming a real job for Arjun, beside you, makes sharing the work ordinary.

scenarios.relearn: Sharing chores teaches boys life skills and lightens the home for everyone.

scenarios.hook: Your office has just announced a new plan to make hiring fairer.
scenarios.setup: You're in the pantry with Manish after lunch.

steps.prompt: Manish mutters: "This plan is unfair to guys like me."

options.text: "Yeah, it's a bit of a raw deal, I guess."
options.then: He nods. You both stew over chai.

options.text: "Stop whining. Women have had it much worse."
options.then: Manish flushes. "So now I'm the problem?"

options.text: "Take it up with HR, not me, please."
options.then: He shrugs and leaves, muttering, "HR won't listen."

options.text: "It widens the pool. The strongest still rise."
options.then: He scoffs. "The strongest? Says who?"

steps.why: Saying the strongest still rise answers the fear without dismissing it.

steps.prompt: The next day Manish asks: "What about the men who were better on paper?"

options.text: "Some men will lose out. That can't be helped."
options.then: Manish folds his arms. "So I was right."

options.text: "Paper means nothing anyway. Forget about paper."
options.then: He laughs. "Then why did I study?"

options.text: "Everyone's scored on the same criteria. It's even."
options.then: Manish slows down. "Same criteria for everyone. That I'd accept."

options.text: "I'll ask the manager to explain it to you."
options.then: The manager is away this week. The question sits.

steps.why: The same criteria for all keeps the plan fair to everyone.

steps.prompt: Later in the week Manish says: "I'd feel better if a few more men sat on the panel."

options.text: "We already have enough men on panels, Manish."
options.then: He frowns. "So we don't count?"

options.text: "Mixed panels help all. Let's suggest it together."
options.then: He brightens. "Together? Okay."

options.text: "Sure, but only if it means less work for me."
options.then: Manish chuckles, and the suggestion is never sent.

options.text: "I'd rather stay out of it now, honestly."
options.then: He nods. The panel stays as it was.

steps.why: Suggesting a mixed panel together makes him a partner in a fair process.

scenarios.relearn: Fair hiring widens the pool so the strongest rise; it helps everyone.

scenarios.hook: At the cricket final, the losing captain breaks down in tears on TV.
scenarios.setup: You're watching it with the lads.

steps.prompt: Bunty laughs: "Look at him crying. Pathetic, yaar."

options.text: "Honestly, letting guys feel things is good for us."
options.then: Bunty pauses. "Good for us? How?"

options.text: "Ha, yeah. Pathetic."
options.then: Bunty grins, and the laughter gets louder.

options.text: "That's disgusting. You're the pathetic one, Bunty."
options.then: Bunty bristles. "Relax. It's a joke."

options.text: "Change the channel, man."
options.then: Someone switches it. The joke is forgotten, and so is the moment.

steps.why: Saying feelings are healthy for guys pushes back gently and stays on his side.

steps.prompt: Later Bunty says quietly: "I felt like crying at my cousin's send-off. Is that weird?"

options.text: "A bit weird, yeah, but fine."
options.then: Bunty laughs awkwardly, and the topic closes.

options.text: "Don't tell the guys. They'll never let it go."
options.then: Bunty nods. Now he thinks the feeling must be hidden.

options.text: "Ask your sister. She'd know about that."
options.then: He shrugs. "Nah." The door closes again.

options.text: "Not weird. It's a big moment. Most people feel it."
options.then: He exhales. "Okay. I thought only I felt that."

steps.why: Telling him it's normal gives him permission to feel, which eases the pressure.

steps.prompt: In the group chat, Bunty posts a crying emoji. A mate replies: "LOL, man up, Bunty."

options.text: "Haha, fair point, bro."
options.then: Bunty goes quiet and stops posting.

options.text: "You're all idiots, honestly."
options.then: The chat fills with insults, and Bunty leaves it.

options.text: "Leave him alone, yaar. We all feel stuff."
options.then: A few thumbs-ups appear. The mate writes, "Okay, okay."

options.text: "Let's talk about something else, guys."
options.then: The chat moves on. Bunty's message is ignored.

steps.why: A short, friendly line backs him up and shows the group a different norm.

scenarios.relearn: Letting men show feeling frees them from a rigid role; it isn't weakness.

scenarios.hook: Your class is running a gender equality workshop, and some boys are hanging back.
scenarios.setup: Kabir stops at the door, arms folded.

steps.prompt: Kabir says: "Equality's a women's thing. Leave us out of it."

options.text: "Fine. Go, then."
options.then: Kabir leaves, and a few others follow him.

options.text: "It's for all of us. A fairer place helps you too."
options.then: He pauses. "Helps me how?"

options.text: "You'll understand when you're a bit older, Kabir."
options.then: He rolls his eyes and walks off.

options.text: "It's not my problem either, honestly."
options.then: Kabir shrugs. "Exactly." You both leave.

steps.why: Saying it's for everyone, with a reason that's his own, brings him in.

steps.prompt: The next day Kabir asks: "What would I even do, if I wanted to help?"

options.text: "Start small. Share chores and listen more."
options.then: He nods. "That I can manage."

options.text: "Just attend the big event and clap."
options.then: He shrugs. Clapping is easy, and nothing else changes.

options.text: "Make a speech about it on the stage."
options.then: He goes pale. "I can't do that."

options.text: "Nothing. Your job is to stay out of the way."
options.then: Kabir frowns. "So I'm just in the way? Great."

steps.why: Small, real actions give him a way in without asking him to perform.

steps.prompt: A week later Kabir says: "My friends already joke that I've gone soft on this stuff."

options.text: "Then you'll have to find better friends, Kabir."
options.then: He frowns. "They're my only friends."

options.text: "Just keep it quiet around them from now on."
options.then: He nods, and the change stays hidden.

options.text: "They'll keep at it. That's how boys are."
options.then: He shrinks. "Then maybe I should stop."

options.text: "Some will joke. Others will notice and may join."
options.then: He smiles nervously. "Maybe Rahul will."

steps.why: Acknowledging the worry, and showing others may join, makes it feel possible.

scenarios.relearn: Equality is everyone's to build; a fairer place is better for them too.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Tanvi has spent the term pushing her club to be fairer, with little to show.
scenarios.setup: You're walking back to the hostel together.

steps.prompt: Tanvi sighs: "Why bother? One fair person won't change anything."

options.text: "You're right. Forget it."
options.then: She nods, and you both feel a little smaller.

options.text: "Stop being so negative about everything, Tanvi."
options.then: She stiffens. "I'm being realistic."

options.text: "Each fair room becomes normal for the next person."
options.then: She thinks. "Normal for the next person. Hm."

options.text: "Then let somebody else do it, I suppose."
options.then: She shrugs. "That's what I thought."

steps.why: Each fair room shows the next person that fairness is possible.

steps.prompt: Tanvi asks: "Has one small change ever actually spread? I've never seen it."

options.text: "Big changes start small. Trust me."
options.then: She smiles thinly. "That's not an example."

options.text: "Our club rotated note-taking. Others copy it now."
options.then: Tanvi raises her eyebrows. "Did they really?"

options.text: "I can't think of one right now, sorry."
options.then: She shrugs, and the doubt stays.

options.text: "Look it up online. There are loads of examples."
options.then: She says, "Sure," and never does.

steps.why: A concrete small example makes 'it adds up' believable.

steps.prompt: The next day Tanvi asks: "What's the smallest thing I could try tomorrow?"

options.text: "Split the next task list so the admin is shared."
options.then: Tanvi nods. "I can do that tomorrow."

options.text: "Start a big campaign across the whole college."
options.then: She groans. "I don't have time for that."

options.text: "Wait until you're in charge of something."
options.then: She sighs. "That's years away."

options.text: "Announce your values to the whole class."
options.then: She winces. "Everyone will think I'm preaching."

steps.why: A small step she can take tomorrow turns 'why bother' into something she can try.

scenarios.relearn: Each fair room you build becomes the new normal for those after you.

scenarios.hook: A peer is rallying people for the campus fairness drive.
scenarios.setup: You're making posters in the common room.

steps.prompt: Ira says: "This drive is us against the boys. Let's make the posters sharp."

options.text: "Yes! Let's make them scared."
options.then: Ira grins. The poster reads like a warning, and the boys at the next table go quiet.

options.text: "Let's not fight at all. Keep it neutral and bland, please."
options.then: Ira shrugs. The posters come out vague, and nobody reads them.

options.text: "Do whatever you like. I'm just helping."
options.then: Ira takes over, and the tone stays sharp.

options.text: "It's with everyone, not against them. That lifts us all."
options.then: Ira frowns. "But they're the ones who hold the power."

steps.why: Saying it's with everyone keeps the drive open to all, boys included.

steps.prompt: Later Ira says: "A few boys want to join. Why let them? They've had it easy."

options.text: "True. They can watch from outside, I suppose."
options.then: Ira nods. The boys stay out, and the drive feels smaller.

options.text: "Fine. Let them do the heavy lifting, then."
options.then: Ira laughs. The boys get stuck carrying boxes and soon drift off.

options.text: "Boys face pressure too. Let's give them real jobs."
options.then: Ira goes quiet. "Some of them did help last year."

options.text: "Let's put it to a vote of the whole group."
options.then: The vote splits the room, and the drive stalls for a week.

steps.why: Inviting boys in, for reasons that are real to them, builds a wider team.

steps.prompt: At the launch, a boy asks Ira: "Can I help at the stall?" Ira looks at you.

options.text: "Sorry, the stall is for girls only."
options.then: The boy nods, hurt, and walks off.

options.text: "Yes, please. We need hands, and ideas too."
options.then: Ira sighs, then hands the boy a stack of flyers.

options.text: "Only if he behaves himself, Ira."
options.then: The boy stiffens. "I wasn't planning to misbehave."

options.text: "Let Ira decide. It's her drive, not mine."
options.then: Ira hesitates, and the boy leaves before she answers.

steps.why: Welcoming him shows that the drive really is with everyone.

scenarios.relearn: A fairness drive is built with everyone, not against the boys; all gain.

scenarios.hook: You're a fresher intern. In standup, a quieter teammate's good idea got skipped over.
