options.then: Sid sends a laughing emoji. The label stays.

options.text: "Sid, that's sexist. Take that back right now."
options.then: Sid bristles. "It was a comment, not a crime."

options.text: "Have you told Nikita that yourself, Sid?"
options.then: Sid replies: "No way." The label stays in the chat.

steps.why: Kindly naming the double standard in the chat changes how the label reads.

steps.prompt: Later, Sid writes: "Anyway, she is a bit much."

options.text: "What did she do that was too much?"
options.then: Sid pauses. "Er. She set a deadline and stuck to it."

options.text: "True. Maybe she could soften it a bit."
options.then: Sid agrees. Her standard gets stricter.

options.text: "Okay. Let's drop it and move on, then."
options.then: The chat moves on. The idea stays unchallenged.

options.text: "You're being really unfair to her, Sid."
options.then: Sid goes defensive. The chat turns tense.

steps.why: Asking for what she actually did turns a label into something you can check.

steps.prompt: Nikita messages you: "Do people think I'm bossy?"

options.text: "One did. That's a double standard, not you."
options.then: Nikita replies: "Thanks for telling me straight."

options.text: "No. Nobody thinks that at all. Honestly."
options.then: Nikita trusts you less when she hears otherwise.

options.text: "A few do. You could smile a bit more."
options.then: Nikita sends a flat "ok". Her confidence dips.

options.text: "Don't worry about what people say. Really."
options.then: Nikita is left guessing what they said.

steps.why: Honesty without drama lets her know, and shows the label isn't about her.

steps.prompt: The lead asks you: "Could you give Nikita some feedback on her leadership?"

options.text: "Yes. I'll focus on what she did."
options.then: The lead nods. Your notes name her results, not her tone.

options.text: "Yes. I'll tell her to tone it down a little."
options.then: Nikita is asked to change how she speaks.

options.text: "Sure. I'll tell her she comes across bossy."
options.then: The label lands in her file.

options.text: "No. It isn't really my place to say."
options.then: The lead finds someone who will use the word.

steps.why: Feedback on what she did, as for anyone, keeps the label out.

scenarios.relearn: The 'bossy' label is the double standard; name it kindly and the same assertiveness reads as leadership.

scenarios.hook: A student comes to see you at the counselling office.
scenarios.setup: Zara sits down, her hands shaking.

steps.prompt: Zara says: "A senior keeps messaging me. I'm scared to say anything."

options.text: "I believe you. It's not your fault."
options.then: Zara's eyes fill. "Thank you. I thought no one would."

options.text: "Are you sure? Maybe don't rock the boat."
options.then: Zara shrinks. "Maybe you're right."

options.text: "Tell me exactly what he wrote, line by line."
options.then: Zara freezes. "I can't say it all out loud."

options.text: "Confront him yourself first. Tell him to stop."
options.then: Zara turns pale. "Alone? He scares me."

steps.why: Believing her first, and saying it isn't her fault, is where support starts.

steps.prompt: Zara says: "I'm afraid of what he'll do if I report."

options.text: "That makes sense. You set the pace."
options.then: Zara relaxes a little. "I don't have to decide today."

options.text: "Reporting can wait until it gets worse."
options.then: Zara nods. The messages keep coming.

options.text: "Let's walk to the committee right now."
options.then: Zara freezes. "Not yet."

options.text: "Just block him and forget all about it."
options.then: Zara blocks him and tells no one. She is carrying it alone.

steps.why: Respecting her pace while staying close keeps her in control.

steps.prompt: Zara asks: "What exactly is the Internal Committee?"

options.text: "It handles harassment complaints. I'll explain."
options.then: Zara listens. "So it's a real route."

options.text: "It's mostly just a formality, honestly."
options.then: Zara's face falls. "So nothing happens."

options.text: "It's only for very serious, proven cases."
options.then: Zara nods. "Then mine doesn't count."

options.text: "You'd have to prove it all before they act."
options.then: Zara goes pale. "I can't prove anything."

steps.why: Plain facts about the route reduce her fear.

steps.prompt: Zara asks: "Is there anyone I can call at night if it gets too much?"

options.text: "Women Helpline 181 is open any hour."
options.then: Zara saves it. "Okay. That helps."

options.text: "Try to sleep it off. It'll feel smaller."
options.then: Zara nods. The nights stay long.

options.text: "Post about it online so people know him."
options.then: Zara looks alarmed. "That could make it worse."

options.text: "Put the phone on silent and ignore it all night."
options.then: Zara nods. She lies awake, still dreading the screen.

steps.why: A helpline she can reach at any hour means she isn't alone.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Zara says: "I think I'm ready to tell the committee."

options.text: "I'll come with you if you'd like."
options.then: Zara nods. "Please."

options.text: "Good. Tell them everything in one go."
options.then: Zara's face tightens. "All at once?"

options.text: "Go on your own. It shows you're serious."
options.then: Zara's voice drops. "I don't want to go alone."

options.text: "Let me write the complaint for you tonight."
options.then: Zara hesitates. "I'd like to say it in my words."

steps.why: Going with her, on her terms, backs her through it. It is never her fault.

scenarios.relearn: Believe her, say it's not her fault, and point to the Internal Committee. That's how you back a target.

scenarios.hook: A friend, Hina, is messaging you late at night.
scenarios.setup: You've just seen her first message.

steps.prompt: Hina texts: "I'm not safe right now. I don't know who to call."

options.text: "I'm here. Call Women Helpline 181, any hour."
options.then: Hina writes: "Okay. Please stay with me."

options.text: "Try to sleep. We'll figure it out tomorrow."
options.then: Hina replies "okay" after a while. She is still alone with it.

options.text: "Tell me everything first. Then we'll decide."
options.then: Hina types, stops and deletes. It's too much tonight.

options.text: "I'll ring your parents for you right now."
options.then: Hina panics. "No. Not them. Please."

steps.why: Staying with her and sharing 181 gives her company and a way to reach help.

steps.prompt: Hina says: "I feel stupid. I should have seen this coming."

options.text: "It's not your fault. I'm glad you told me."
options.then: Hina's typing pauses. "Thank you."

options.text: "Why didn't you leave earlier, honestly?"
options.then: Hina goes silent.

options.text: "Don't be silly. It could be a lot worse."
options.then: Hina sends a flat "ok".

options.text: "You should have known the signs earlier."
options.then: Hina replies "I know" and stops.

steps.why: Saying it isn't her fault, and that you're glad she told you, lifts the shame.

steps.prompt: Hina says: "I'm not ready to call anyone. Can you just stay on the chat?"

options.text: "I'll stay. Women Helpline 181 is open any hour."
options.then: Hina writes: "Thank you. That helps."

options.text: "You really have to call someone tonight, Hina."
options.then: Hina panics. She stops replying.

options.text: "Then I'll make the call for you right now, Hina."
options.then: Hina writes: "No, please. I want to choose."

options.text: "I can't stay up. Message me again tomorrow."
options.then: Hina goes offline. She is alone again.

steps.why: Staying close, and keeping help within reach, respects her pace.

steps.prompt: The next morning, Hina writes: "I called. They listened. What now?"

options.text: "Thank you for telling me. What do you need?"
options.then: Hina writes: "Just someone to sit with. Can you?"

options.text: "Great. Now you can put it all behind you."
options.then: Hina goes quiet. The worry is still there.

options.text: "So what did they say? Tell me all of it."
options.then: Hina hesitates. She wanted to keep some of it private.

options.text: "Tell everyone you know so they understand."
options.then: Hina's stomach drops. She wanted to choose who knows.

steps.why: Asking what she needs keeps the next step hers.

scenarios.relearn: For a woman in distress, share Women Helpline 181 and stay present. It's open any hour.

scenarios.hook: In your friend group, a "joke" lands on the one woman present.
scenarios.setup: Everyone laughs except Tia.

steps.prompt: Sid says, grinning: "Tia can't carry that. She's a girl!"

options.text: "That one's not on, mate. Let's leave it."
options.then: Sid blinks. "Okay. Fine."

options.text: "Ha. Steady on, Sid. Next round's on you."
options.then: Everyone laughs. Tia looks at her phone.

options.text: "Dude, you're honestly such a sexist, Sid."
options.then: Sid bristles. "It's a joke."

options.text: "Tia, just ignore him. He's a bit of an idiot."
options.then: Tia forces a smile. The joke has gone unanswered.

steps.why: A light, clear line names it without a fight.

steps.prompt: Sid says: "Come on. It's just banter."

options.text: "Banter works when everyone's in on it."
options.then: Sid pauses. "Tia, was that okay?"

options.text: "Fair enough. It's just banter, isn't it."
options.then: Sid grins. Tia says nothing.

options.text: "Fine. But you're on thin ice, mate."
options.then: Sid rolls his eyes. The mood sours.

options.text: "Whatever. Let's just drop it, yeah."
options.then: The group moves on. The joke stays in the air.

steps.why: Saying banter needs everyone in on it explains the effect without an attack.

steps.prompt: Tia tells you later: "I never know whether to say something when it happens."

options.text: "It's your call. I'll back you either way."
options.then: Tia nods. "That helps. I don't want to do it alone."

options.text: "You should always say something right then."
options.then: Tia looks tired. "It's not that simple."

options.text: "Never bother. They never change anyway."
options.then: Tia nods. She stays silent next time.

options.text: "I'll handle all of it from now on, Tia."
options.then: Tia frowns. "I'd like to have a say."

steps.why: Leaving the choice to her and offering steady backing supports her.

scenarios.relearn: Name a sexist 'joke' lightly but clearly; laughing along leaves it on the person it targets.

scenarios.hook: In a seminar you have a half-formed idea but worry it's not polished enough.
scenarios.setup: You're near the front, your notebook open.

steps.prompt: Professor Nair says: "Anyone have a thought before we move on?"

options.text: "It's half-formed, but here's where I'd start..."
options.then: Nair nods. "Go on. Half-formed is fine."

options.text: "I'll bring it next week when it's polished."
options.then: Nair nods. "Next week, then." The moment passes.

options.text: "Sorry, this is probably a silly idea, but..."
options.then: Nair smiles. Your idea is framed as silly before it starts.

options.text: "Rahul should go first. He's better at this."
options.then: Rahul starts. Your idea stays in your notebook.

steps.why: A half-formed thought is still worth voicing. You belong in the conversation.

steps.prompt: In the next seminar, Professor Nair says: "Who'd like to open today?"

options.text: "I'll open. It's rough, but it's a start."
options.then: Nair nods. "Excellent. The floor is yours."

options.text: "I'll wait until I've read it once more."
options.then: Nair nods. Another student opens.

options.text: "Can someone else start? I'll add after."
options.then: A student opens. You add nothing before the bell.

options.text: "Only if nobody else wants to open today."
options.then: Two hands go up. You put yours down.

steps.why: Volunteering a rough start builds the habit of speaking first.

steps.prompt: After class, you tell Rahul your reading. He says: "That's not how the text goes."

options.text: "Maybe. Where do you see it differently?"
options.then: Rahul explains. You refine your point aloud.

options.text: "Oh, you're probably right. Forget it then."
options.then: You drop the idea, and it goes no further.

options.text: "Have you even read it properly, Rahul?"
options.then: Rahul stiffens. "Yes, actually."

options.text: "It's my reading of it. That's final."
options.then: Rahul raises an eyebrow. The discussion ends.

steps.why: Staying curious keeps you in the conversation without backing down.

scenarios.relearn: A half-formed thought is still worth voicing; you belong in the conversation before it's perfect.
